issues.legal_issue: A compromise affecting minors may be set aside for gross negligence when the guardian’s concessions are one-sided and the court grants leave without adequately considering the relevant circumstances.
material_facts: Some of the decree-holders in the pending appeal were minors represented by a guardian.
The compromise set aside the entire trial decree, including eviction relief and an award of arrears of rent and damages, and dismissed the suit.
The stated consideration for the compromise was that the tenants gave up a possible claim for costs if they succeeded in the appeal.
No ground was identified on which the money award could successfully be challenged, and the court considered that the award was significant in light of the circumstances.
The effect of a housing law that came into force during the litigation was not meaningfully considered by the minors’ advocate or the court when leave to compromise was granted.
The courts below found that the guardian was grossly negligent in failing to take the minors’ interests into account.
issues.conclusion: The compromise decree was properly set aside for gross negligence, and the Supreme Court did not interfere with that decision. The pending appeal was restored for disposal in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXXII, Rule 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure requires the court to grant a guardian leave to compromise on behalf of a minor only after considering all relevant circumstances. The court applied that requirement to the one-sided compromise and the failure to assess the minors’ interests. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: challenge_to_compromise_decree_involving_minors and court_approved_guardian_compromise and minors_surrendered_existing_decree_rights and consideration_was_only_possible_costs and money_award_had_no_identified_challenge_ground and waived_costs_were_small_relative_to_surrendered_rights and relevant_change_in_law_was_not_assessed

predicates.challenge_to_compromise_decree_involving: A party brought a proceeding challenging a compromise decree made on behalf of minor parties.
predicates.court_approved_guardian_compromise: The court granted permission for the minors’ guardian to enter into the compromise.
predicates.minors_surrendered_existing_decree_right: The minors gave up rights awarded to them under an existing decree, including substantive relief and a money award.
predicates.consideration_was_only_possible_costs: The only stated benefit to the minors was the opposing parties’ waiver of costs they might possibly have obtained.
predicates.money_award_had_no_identified_challenge_: No ground was identified on which the existing money award could successfully be challenged.
predicates.waived_costs_were_small_relative_to_surr: The possible costs waived were not substantial in comparison with the rights the minors surrendered.
predicates.relevant_change_in_law_was_not_assessed: The effect of a change in law relevant to the pending appeal was not meaningfully considered before the compromise was approved.

issues.definition: When a challenged compromise for minors, approved by the court, makes the minors surrender existing decree rights for only possible costs, with no identified basis to challenge the money award, the costs small relative to those rights, and a relevant change in law unassessed, the compromise decree is set aside for the guardian’s gross negligence.
